title: Should 1 Thess 2:16 move into the row 'Who is saved'?

why: The verse says Paul was hindered from "telling the Gentiles how they may be saved", which is about preaching and does not say who is saved, and 'Who is saved' is the one row the two reading halves dispute.

title: Should the 'Who is saved' heading name neither side first?

The earlier draft's "the chosen" is replaced by 2 Thess 2:13's own words, because that verse does not say "the chosen".
why: Rom 9:27 "only the remnant will be saved" and Rom 11:26 "all Israel will be saved" then each stand as their own words, and listing them in the Bible's order puts neither side first.

title: Should 'Salvation is the LORD's' be folded into 'God and salvation'?

title: Should the 'Savior' row join 'The LORD saves the afflicted'?

title: Should the cross row be merged into 'Not saved'?

after: No change.
why: Matt 27:42 "He saved others, but He cannot save Himself" is the mockers' words at one scene, and folding it in beside God not saving ("You do not save?", Hab 1:2) would draw a line the page does not draw.

title: Should the Jude 5 note say the Greek reads 'Lord'?

why: Titus 1:3 says "God our Savior" and 1:4 "Christ Jesus our Savior", and Titus 2:13 and 2 Pet 1:1 each join "God" and "Savior" under one article, which readers take of one person or of two.

title: Should the first row's note point to the Red Sea rescue?

title: Does 'a Master in heaven' (Eph 6:9, Col 4:1) name Jesus?

title: Should Matt 23:9 move into 'Your heavenly Father; My heavenly Father'?

title: Should Deut 10:14 be shown first in 'Heaven is God's throne'?

why: Deut 10:14 "to the LORD your God belong the heavens, even the highest heavens" and 1 Kgs 8:27 "cannot contain You" show the heading's "belong to Him" and "cannot contain Him", while Rev 11:19 stays fourth as the only one showing "the temple in heaven".

title: Should Dan 7:13 get its own row apart from Jesus?
now: Dan 7:13 is one of the 16 verses in the row headed 'Taken up into heaven (...); coming with the clouds of heaven or from heaven: "One like the Son of Man", "the Son of Man", "the Lord Jesus", "His Son"', whose card link goes to Jesus.

why: Dan 7:13 "One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven" gets its own words and first place, while a one-verse row would hide that Matt 24:30 and Mark 14:62 repeat the phrase "coming with the clouds of heaven".

title: Should Ezek 8:3 leave the 'Holy Spirit and heaven' row?

after: Ezek 8:3 leaves that row (6 verses remain), the heading loses ", lifting up between earth and heaven", and the note loses its sentence about Ezek 8:3 while keeping the Luke 11:13 and Heb 6:4 sentences. The verse stays in 'In heaven and on earth'.
why: Ezek 8:3 has only "the Spirit lifted me up" (Hebrew rûaḥ, no "Holy"), a noun and not a pronoun resolved by its clause, so the new rule does not turn it into the Holy Spirit and nothing is lost since the verse stays in the heaven-and-earth row.

title: Should Rom 10:6 leave the 'came down from heaven' row?

title: Matt 23:9 again: should it move into the Father row?

after: The same move as item 15: Matt 23:9 goes into the Father row, whose heading gains "you have one Father, who is in heaven" (Matt 23:9), and leaves the 'Heavenly realms' row. Applying one settles both items.

title: Should Deut 28:3-6 stay in 'The LORD your God will bless you'?

title: Should Eph 1:3 leave the 'God blessed' row?

title: Should 1 Cor 10:16 leave the nouns' 'Every other use' row?

title: Should the Abraham row's note point to Gen 12:2 and Gal 3:14?

title: Should Ps 67:6-7 move into the 'God blessed' row?

title: Should Mark 14:61 leave the 'People bless God' row?

title: Should 1 Cor 10:16 leave the “Jesus blessed” row?

title: Should Jer 17:7 stay in both of its places?

title: Should Ps 83:5 move out of the covenants between peoples?

title: Should Dan 9:27 move out of the blood-and-cup row?

title: Should Isa 42:6 be shown on the covenant page?

title: Should the covenant page note its marriage verses?

title: Should Mal 3:1 move into the Levi and priests row?

title: Should the card be named “law (Torah) and instruction”?

why: Only one row is about the instruction sense (Isa 5:24 “the instruction of the LORD of Hosts”, Prov 1:8), so a card called “instruction” alone shows one sense as the whole.

title: Should the law rows point to the “instruction” verses?

Isa 1:10 (“listen to the instruction of our God”) is left out of the rejecting note because it is not a rejection, and Isa 2:3 stays where it is.
why: Isa 5:24 says “rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts” in the same Hebrew word the law rows treat, but moving it would put the instruction sense under rows labelled “the law”, so only pointers go in.

title: Should the “Died to the law” row change?

after: No change. Rom 10:4 stays in this row only, and the label stays long (the editor can still shorten it).

title: Should “Jesus speaks of the law” change places?
now: The row “Jesus speaks of the law: “I have not come to abolish”, “in your own Law”, “not one of you keeps it”” comes after the three side-by-side rows and before the closing list of other uses. Its first four verses shown are Matt 5:17, John 8:17, John 7:19 and John 10:34.
after: No change.
why: Before the three rows Jesus’ words (“I have not come to abolish”) read as the premise of Paul’s, and after them as the ending, so either place tilts, and the list of other uses must stay last in any case.

title: Should “Taught and read aloud” be split in two?
now: The row “Taught and read aloud; the priests, Levites, scribes and Pharisees” holds 59 verses, and the law page has 26 rows.
after: No change.
why: A split would make 27 rows against the aim of 15 to 25, and a note pointing to Heb 7:12 (“the law must be changed as well”) would pull readers into the contested rows.

title: Should the faith row and the works row be merged?
now: “The law, and faith, believing” and “The law, and works” sit side by side, and a verse that names both (Rom 3:28, Gal 2:16) shows in both.
after: No change.
why: The two rows stand on different Greek words, faith (πίστις) and works (ἔργον), and one merged row would show Paul’s contrast as a single frame.

title: Should the law page show the Old Testament’s own sequence?
now: Gen 26:5, Deut 31:24, 2 Kgs 22:8, Neh 8:1, Jer 31:33, Isa 2:3, Ps 119:44 and Mal 4:4 already show in the Torah rows, in the Old Testament’s own order. The row “Before the law was given…” has no note about that sequence.
after: No change.
why: A note on one of the three contested rows would break their matching shape, and setting Ps 119:44 (“I will always obey Your law, forever and ever”) beside Heb 7:19 or Rom 10:4 would weigh one side.

title: Should Heb 10:26 move beside Mark 3:29?
now: Heb 10:26 is the last verse of the row “If someone sins”: the Law’s cases, sinning unintentionally; sinning defiantly (Num 15:30); sinning deliberately (Heb 10:26)”, and its note says it is a verse of Hebrews and not a case of the Law. The row on a sin to death and a sin not forgiven (1 John 5:16-17, Matt 12:31, Mark 3:28-29) has a note that points to Heb 10:26.
after: No change.
why: Heb 10:26 says “no further sacrifice for sins remains” and does not say the sin is unforgiven, while Mark 3:29 says it “will never be forgiven”, so setting them together would take a side on whether a believer can fall away.

title: Should the golden calf get its own row on the sin page?
now: No row gathers the calf scene. Exod 32:30 and 32:32 show in “Sin forgiven, atoned for, covered…”, and Exod 32:21, 32:31, 32:34 and Deut 9:18, 9:21 show only in the list of other uses at the bottom of the nouns section; the page has 24 rows.
after: A new row, “The calf at Sinai: “a great sin”, “their sin”, “that sinful thing””, shows Exod 32:21, 32:30, 32:31, 32:32, 32:34 and Deut 9:18, 9:21 (32:30 and 32:32 also stay in the “forgiven” row; the other five leave the list of other uses), taking the page to 25 rows. There is no “Sin first named” row and no Day of Atonement row.
why: Moses says “You have committed a great sin” (Exod 32:30) and the neighbouring verses name the same sin, so one scene is scattered, but “Sin first named” would not be true of its verses since Gen 4:7 is the first noun and Gen 20:6 the first verb.

title: Should the 27 Levitical verses leave the “forgiven” row?
now: The row “Sin forgiven, atoned for, covered, wiped away, cleansed, taken away” includes 27 verses of Leviticus and Numbers that also show in “The sin offering; a sacrifice for sin”, for example Lev 4:20.
after: No change.
why: Lev 4:20 says “the priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven”, so the verse fits both rows by its own words, and taking it out would split forgiveness from sacrifice.

title: Should “Christ and our sins” point to Isaiah 53 and the goat?
now: The note under “Christ and our sins: “save His people from their sins”…” does not mention Isa 53:12 or Lev 16:21. Isa 53:12 shows in “Sin and its consequence…”, and Lev 16:21 in “Confessing sin” and in “Sin beside iniquity…”.
after: The note gets one sentence: 1 Pet 2:24 says He “bore our sins”; Isa 53:12 says “He bore the sin of many” and Lev 16:21 puts the sins “on the goat’s head”; those two verses show in the rows named above, and the page does not say how the three relate. No verse moves, and the wording that where verses “quote or echo” they say so is not used.
why: “Bore” and “sin” stand in 1 Pet 2:24, Isa 53:12 and the goat verse, so a pointer is plain text, but 1 Pet 2:24 does not say it quotes Isaiah, so a sentence saying so would claim a link the verse does not state.

title: Should “against You” prayers count as sinning against the LORD?
now: The row “Sinned against the LORD, against God” holds only verses that name him themselves. Ps 51:4 (“Against You, You only, have I sinned”), Ps 119:11, 1 Kgs 8:33, 8:46 and 2 Chr 6:24 say only “You”, so they show in other rows, and the note under the row lists them as “against You” verses found elsewhere.
after: Three of them now count as naming the LORD because the name is close by: Ps 51:4 (“O God” in 51:1, the same prayer), Ps 119:11 (“O LORD” in the next verse, 119:12) and 1 Kgs 8:46 (“pray to the LORD” two verses earlier, 8:44). Each shows in the row beside the verse that names him and stays in its other row, and the note under the row is reworded; 1 Kgs 8:33 and 2 Chr 6:24 stay out, since Solomon’s prayer names the LORD there only five verses back (1 Kgs 8:28; 2 Chr 6:19).
why: Ps 119:11 says “sin against You” right beside “Blessed are You, O LORD” in 119:12, so under the new rule it names him, while 1 Kgs 8:33 and 2 Chr 6:24 are five verses from the name.

title: Should 1 Cor 8:12 and Luke 15:18, 21 leave “Sinned against another”?
now: The row “Sinned against another: a neighbor, a brother, one’s own body” shows 1 Cor 8:12 (“you sin against Christ”) and Luke 15:18 and 15:21 (“against heaven and against you”); its note says the page lets those words stand.
after: No change.
why: 1 Cor 8:12 begins “By sinning against your brothers in this way” and Luke 15:18 says “against heaven and against you” of the father, so each also holds a sin against another person, and moving them would drop that.

title: Should the kidney-word verses leave the “LORD searches the heart” row?
now: The row “The LORD, God, searches, tests and knows the heart” shows Ps 7:9, Ps 26:2, Jer 11:20 and Jer 20:12, where the Berean’s “heart and mind” prints the Hebrew word for kidneys as “heart” and the heart word as “mind”. Ps 7:9 and Jer 11:20 also show under “Other words translated heart”, with a note that the page does not make the two words one.
after: No change.
why: Each verse names the LORD or God and has the Hebrew heart word beside the kidney word, as in Jer 11:20’s “examines the heart and mind”, so it is a heart verse and the note already says the two words are not made one.

title: Should the Rom 2:29 note be reworded?
now: In the row “In believers’ hearts: the Spirit, Christ, the peace of God; cleansed by faith” the note ends with the sentence “In Rom 2:29 ‘circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code’.” The verse is in the row.
after: That last sentence is replaced by: “Rom 2:29 says who is a Jew inwardly, and that circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code; it speaks of the Jew and of the written code, and the page takes no side on how Paul’s words apply to believers.” The verse stays in the row.
why: The verse says “a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly” and does not mention believers, so the row’s heading alone would say more than the verse does (the Greek word behind “Spirit” also has no “the”, which is why the sentence keeps the Berean’s words).

title: Should Dan 7:28 be a verse of the “Says, thinks” row?
now: Dan 7:28 shows only under “Other words translated heart”, with a note that the Berean prints “But I kept the matter to myself” and the Aramaic reads “in my heart”.
after: No change.
why: The Berean prints “But I kept the matter to myself” with no word for heart, so in the “Says, thinks, plans” row it would show a verse that does not show its heading, and moving it also needs a change to how the site reads the Aramaic word.

title: Should the Rev 2:23 note say the Greek is “kidneys and hearts”?
now: Rev 2:23 (“I am the One who searches minds and hearts”) shows in “Jesus knows their hearts…”, and the note there does not say that the Berean’s “minds” is the Greek word for kidneys; the page says so only under “Other words translated heart”.
after: The note under “Jesus knows their hearts” gets one sentence: the Greek is “kidneys and hearts” (νεφροὺς καὶ καρδίας) where the Berean prints “minds and hearts”, with a pointer to “Other words translated heart”. Nothing is put in the LORD row or the Jesus row pointing to the other.
why: The Greek pairs kidneys and hearts as Jer 17:10 pairs the Hebrew words, so the sentence is plain text, but a pointer between the two rows would say the page reads Rev 2:23 as the LORD’s words of Jer 17:10, which it keeps apart on purpose.

title: Should five verses leave the “In believers’ hearts” row?
now: The row “In believers’ hearts: the Spirit, Christ, the peace of God; cleansed by faith” shows 1 John 3:19, 3:20, 3:21, Eph 5:19 and Col 2:2, and its note has a sentence on 1 John 3:19-21. Those 1 John verses also show in “Troubled, broken, faint or afraid…”, Eph 5:19 in “Beside loving, seeking, praying, praising and giving thanks”, and Col 2:2 in the wisdom row.
after: 1 John 3:19, 3:20, 3:21 and Col 2:2 leave the row, and the 1 John 3:19-21 sentence leaves its note; each still shows in its other row. Eph 5:19 stays, because “sing and make music in your hearts to the Lord” sits between “be filled with the Spirit” (5:18) and “our Lord Jesus Christ” (5:20).
why: 1 John 3:19-21 (“God is greater than our hearts”) is about a heart that condemns and Col 2:2 (“encouraged in heart”) has no one living in the heart, but Eph 5:19’s “the Lord” is named in 5:20 as “our Lord Jesus Christ”, so the new rule keeps it.

title: Should 1 John 3:20 go in the “LORD searches the heart” row?
now: 1 John 3:20 (“God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things”) shows in “Troubled, broken, faint or afraid…” and, until the item above is settled, in “In believers’ hearts”. It is not in “The LORD, God, searches, tests and knows the heart”.
after: No change.
why: “He” is plainly God here, but the verse says God “knows all things”, not that he searches, tests or knows the heart, which is what that row’s heading says of every verse in it (Luke 16:15: “God knows your hearts”).

title: Should 'Weary of life' be folded into 'The present life'?
now: On the life page, under 'What the text says of life', the row 'Weary of life: “I am weary of my life”, “I despise my own life”, “I hated life”, “better for me to die than to live”' stands on its own with 8 verses (Gen 27:46, Job 3:20, 9:21, 10:1, Eccl 2:17, Jonah 4:3, 4:8, 1 Kgs 19:4), apart from the 19-verse row 'The present life: how short it is...'.
after: No change.
why: 'I am weary of my life' (Gen 27:46) and 'better for me to die than to live' (Jonah 4:3) are laments, a third voice beside the length of a life and what one has to live on, and a merge would only take the page from 30 rows to 29.

title: Should the row 'Life held out' be renamed 'Phrases with life'?
now: The row headed 'Life held out: “the promise: eternal life”, “the crown of life”, “the word of life”, “the full message of this new life”, “the gracious gift of life”, “the life of God”' holds 9 verses, and the first four shown are 1 John 2:25, Jas 1:12, Phil 2:16 and Acts 5:20.
after: The row keeps its 9 verses and is not merged into 'The path of life'; its heading becomes 'Phrases with “life”: “the promise: eternal life”, “the crown of life”, “the word of life”, “the full message of this new life”, “the gracious gift of life”, “the life of God”', so only the words 'Life held out' go.
why: 'Held out' is the page's word, not the text's, and it leans toward 'not yet' beside Jas 1:12 ('the crown of life that God has promised') although Eph 4:18 speaks of being 'alienated from the life of God'.

title: Should 'The years one lived' be merged with 'The days of life'?
now: Under 'Living, and making alive' the row 'The years one lived: “lived 140 years”, “was 90 years old”' (44 verses) is separate from the row 'The days of life, the years of life, a lifetime, a long life' (52 verses) under 'What the text says of life', and Gen 47:28 stands in both.
after: No change.
why: Gen 47:28 says both 'Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years' and 'the length of his life was 147 years', so it already sits in each row where it fits.

title: Which of the proposed splits of the life rows should be made?
now: John 3:15 and 3:16 ('may have eternal life', 'shall not perish but have eternal life') are in no row, only in the 208-verse list of other uses at the bottom of 'What the text says of life' (John 3:16 is also shown among the verses at the head of the page); John 5:40 and 20:31 ('may have life') are only in 'Christ and life', and John 6:40 only in 'Now and later in the same verse'. The breath, fountain, 'life laid down' and 'dead live again' rows are each one long row, and the breath row has a link to the Holy Spirit page but no note.
after: A new row headed 'Having life, eternal life: “may have eternal life”, “shall not perish but have eternal life”, “to have life”, “you may have life in His name”' holds John 3:15, 3:16, 5:40, 6:40 and 20:31 with the usual 'the page takes no side' sentence; John 6:40 leaves 'Now and later in the same verse', and the notes of the three other eternal-life rows point to the new one (the page goes from 30 rows to 31). The other splits are not made: the breath row gets a note that Gen 2:7, 7:22 and Job 12:10 say 'breath' without saying it is the Spirit while Rom 8:2, 8:6 and John 6:63 name the Spirit; the fountain heading is cut to 'A fountain, water, bread, light “of life”; and things called “living”' with a line that these are different words; the 'life laid down' row shows 1 Kgs 19:10, 1 Sam 22:23, Ps 35:4 and John 10:11 first and takes in Luke 17:33, Gen 12:13, Job 2:4, 2:6, Esth 7:3 and 1 Sam 26:21 from the list of other uses; and the 'dead live again' row gets notes on Rev 13:14 (the beast 'wounded by the sword and yet had lived') and Luke 15:24, 32 (a father speaking of his son).
why: John 3:16, the page's own key verse, sits in no row, and a fourth eternal-life row for the 'have' verses the other three leave out fixes that, while splitting the other rows would take a 30-row page to 33.

title: Should the 'God makes alive' row link to the Jesus page?
now: Under 'Living, and making alive', the row 'God makes alive, revives, gives life: ...' (34 verses) links to the pages on God, the Holy Spirit, the resurrection, preserving life and prayer, but not to the Jesus page.
after: The same row also links to the Jesus page; no verse is put in or taken out.
why: John 5:21 ('so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes') and Eph 2:5 ('made us alive with Christ') already name the Son and Christ in the verse, and no reader objected.

title: Which clean-ups of repeated verses and notes on life go ahead?
now: Four verses where the Berean prints 'long life' for the Hebrew word for 'days' (1 Kgs 3:11, 2 Chr 1:11, Job 12:12, Ps 91:16) stand in 'The days of life, the years of life...'; John 5:39 and 6:54 stand in 'Eternal life, said as had or given now'; Ps 18:46 and 2 Sam 22:47 ('The LORD lives') stand in the oaths row; and the notes on Exod 21:23, John 6:53 and the 'Live by the commandments' row are as first written.
after: Eight changes: (1) the four 'long life' verses leave the days row and stay only in the list of other words at the bottom, under the Hebrew word for 'day'; (2) John 5:39 ('you presume that by them you possess eternal life') leaves the 'had or given now' row and falls to the list of other uses; (3) John 6:54 leaves that row and stays in 'Now and later in the same verse'; (4) Ps 18:46 and 2 Sam 22:47 move to 'The living God; He who lives forever' (the Hebrew words shown under Ps 18:46 belong to the neighbouring verse because of the Hebrew numbering), and the oaths row gets a line that Amos 8:14 swears by other gods ('your god, O Dan') while Hos 4:15 forbids swearing 'As surely as the LORD lives' at Gilgal and Beth-aven; (5) the note under the verb section's list of other uses says that verses with the word 'living' are in the noun rows; (6) the note under 'A life for a life' says Jewish readers of the rabbinic period take Exod 21:23-25 as payment of compensation and the page takes no side (the wording to be checked against the Mekhilta); (7) the John 6:53 note says it is read 'as the Eucharist (the Lord's Supper), as faith in Christ, or as both'; (8) the note under 'Live by the commandments' says, Hebrew first, that Lev 18:5, Deut 4:1, 5:33, 8:1 and 30:16 give the commandments that Israel may live and that Paul quotes Lev 18:5 in Gal 3:12 (just after Hab 2:4 in 3:11) and in Rom 10:5. Rom 6:22 and the other repeated verses stay where they are.
why: Both review halves agree on the four 'long life' verses (the Hebrew word is 'days'), on John 5:39 and on John 6:54, while Rom 6:22 ('the outcome is eternal life') stays because a verse sits in every row it fits.

title: Should 'Christ died' be merged into 'The death of Christ'?
now: On the death page, 'Christ died' (12 verses such as Rom 5:6, 5:8 and 1 Cor 15:3, under 'Dying, and being put to death') and 'The death of Christ' (10 verses such as Rom 5:10, 6:3, Heb 2:9 and 1 Cor 11:26, under 'What the text says of death') are two rows that share no verse.
after: No change.
why: 'Christ died for the ungodly' (Rom 5:6) uses the verb and 'through the death of His Son' (Rom 5:10) the noun, two different Greek words, so this is not one thing recorded twice.

title: Should Rom 6:4 and 6:9 leave 'Jesus Christ raised from the dead'?
now: Rom 6:4 and 6:9 stand in the row 'Jesus Christ raised from the dead' (25 verses, under 'The dead') and also in the row 'Death and the resurrection', which opens with Isa 26:19 and Dan 12:2.
after: No change.
why: Rom 6:4 and 6:9 both say 'Christ was raised from the dead', naming him in the verse, and the other row holds the Old Testament hope (Isa 26:19, Dan 12:2, Ezek 37:12-13) first.

title: Which fixes to the rows on Christ's death should be made?
now: 'The death of Christ' includes 2 Tim 1:10 and Heb 5:7, and its note ends its list of what the death does with the word 'communes'; the rows 'Christ died' and 'Jesus Christ raised from the dead' do not point to it or to each other, and the second has no note.
after: 2 Tim 1:10 leaves 'The death of Christ' and stays in 'Death as ruler and enemy'; in the note 'communes' becomes 'unites us to Him'; and a see-also line naming the other two rows goes into the notes of 'Christ died', 'The death of Christ' and 'Jesus Christ raised from the dead'. Heb 5:7 is not moved and stays in both 'The death of Christ' and 'Delivered from death'.
why: 2 Tim 1:10 says Christ Jesus 'has abolished death' and says nothing of his own death, so under 'The death of Christ' it would state how death is abolished, while Rom 6:5 ('united with Him like this in His death') supports 'unites us to Him'.

title: Should 'The LORD brings death' point to Ezek 18:23 and 33:11?
now: The row 'The LORD brings death and gives life' (12 verses, under 'Dying, and being put to death') has only 1 Sam 2:6 and Deut 32:39 saying 'gives life'; Ezek 18:23 and 33:11, where the LORD speaks of the death of the wicked, are in another row, 'The death of the wicked, of the righteous, of His saints', and nothing points from one to the other.
after: One sentence goes into the note under 'The LORD brings death and gives life': Ezek 18:23 and 33:11, where the LORD speaks of the death of the wicked, are in the row 'The death of the wicked, of the righteous, of His saints'. No verse moves.
why: Ezek 33:11 ('turn from their ways and live') is the LORD speaking of death and life but stands in another row, and a pointer names where without softening any hard verse.

title: Should the bread words of the Last Supper join 'The Lord's table'?
now: Under 'What the text says of sacrifice', the row 'The Lord's table: blood “poured out”, “in remembrance of Me”, “a participation”' holds 8 verses (Matt 26:28, Luke 22:19-20, 1 Cor 10:16, 10:18, 10:21, 11:24-25), and its note says the bread words of Matt 26:26-27 and Mark 14:22-24 are not set there.
after: Matt 26:26 and Mark 14:22 ('this is My body') come into the row, with Mark 14:24 beside Matt 26:28 so Mark's telling is whole; 'This is My body' goes into the heading, and the note's sentence about what is left out is corrected to name only what still is (Matt 26:27, 1 Cor 11:23, 26). Heb 13:10 ('We have an altar') stays out.
why: Luke 22:19 ('This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me') is already in the row with no sacrifice word, and Matt 26:26 and Mark 14:22 say the same words of the same supper and name Jesus, while Heb 13:10 names no table and no supper.

title: Should the Hebrews row point to what the law's offerings did?
now: The row 'Hebrews: offered again and again, unable to cleanse; once for all' (8 verses, Heb 7:27 to 10:14) sets Heb 9:9 and 10:1 against the law's offerings, and its note does not say what the law itself says those offerings were given for.
after: One sentence goes into the note under that row: the rows above say what the law's offerings were given for, for example the priest 'will make atonement for that man's sin, and he will be forgiven' (Lev 4:26); it says nothing on how that stands to Heb 9:9 or 10:1.
why: Lev 4:26 shows what the Torah itself says an offering did, so a reader does not take the Hebrews row for the whole account, and as a bare pointer it sets the two side by side without choosing.

title: Row or note for the dedication of the altar and temple?
now: Num 7:88, 1 Kgs 8:63 and 2 Chr 7:5 each stand in other rows (the animals row and the peace-offering row, and for 1 Kgs 8:63 also 'Sacrificed to the LORD'; 2 Chr 7:5 is in the verb section's list of other uses), and the note under 'Every other use: sacrifice, offering' names only the dedication of the temple in 2 Chr 7.
after: No 25th row is made; the note under 'Every other use: sacrifice, offering' names the dedications together: Num 7:88 ('the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed'), 1 Kgs 8:63 ('the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD') and 2 Chr 7:5 ('the king and all the people dedicated the house of God').
why: All three say it in the text's own words, but a three-verse row would put a 24-row page at the top of its 15-25 range for verses that already show elsewhere.

title: Should John 1:29, the Lamb of God, get a row or note?
now: John 1:29 ('Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!') is not on the sacrifice page, which holds only verses with a word for sacrifice or offering; the Passover row and the Hebrews row link to the 'Lamb of God' pages.
after: No change.
why: John 1:29 names Jesus ('John saw Jesus coming toward him') but has no word for sacrifice or offering, and any row or note would decide which lamb it means, while the existing links already give the reader the verse.

title: Should the two verb rows on works and faith be merged?
now: Under 'Who judges whom', the row 'Judged, and works, deeds, ways' comes first and 'Judged, and believing, faith' directly after it, and the two notes say 'Set beside the next row' and 'Set beside the row before'.
after: The two rows stay separate, with 'Judged, and believing, faith' first and 'Judged, and works, deeds, ways' second, and both notes say 'These two rows are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking' (the wording the blood page uses). The noun pair 'Judgment and works, deeds' and 'Condemnation, and “no condemnation”' could take the same sentence only if 'Condemnation' is put first, since they are not in alphabetical order now.
why: John 3:18 ('Whoever believes in Him is not condemned') and Rev 20:12 ('judged according to their deeds') sit in the two rows and 2 Thess 2:12 joins unbelief and delight in wickedness in one verse, so a merge would join the very pair the page leaves open.

title: Should Ps 1:5 also stand in 'In the gate and the court'?
now: Ps 1:5 ('the wicked will not stand in the judgment') stands in the row 'The day of judgment, the hour of judgment...' and not in 'In the gate and the court'; the day row has no note.
after: Ps 1:5 stays in the day-of-judgment row and also appears in 'In the gate and the court', and a note under the day row says Ps 1:5 is read of a court and of the last day and the page does not choose.
why: Ps 1:5 names neither a court nor a day, only that the wicked 'will not stand in the judgment', so showing it in both rows moves it without settling which it is.

title: Should texts with no word for judgment get rows or a pointer?
now: The page holds only verses that use a word for judgment, so Joel 1:15, Amos 5:18, Zeph 1:14 and Isa 13:9 ('the Day of the LORD') and the sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46) are not on it, and the day-of-judgment row has no note and no link to the wrath page.
after: No new rows are made; the day-of-judgment row gets a link to the wrath page and a note: the Hebrew 'Day of the LORD' texts (Joel 1:15, Amos 5:18, Zeph 1:14, Isa 13:9) use other words and are not on this page, Isa 13:13 and Zeph 1:15 are on the wrath page, Amos 5:18 is on the light page, and the sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46) is gathered with this page.
why: Joel 1:15 ('the Day of the LORD is near') and the others speak of destruction or darkness with no word for judgment, and filing Matt 25:46 or 1 Cor 3:15 here would put one side's proof-texts on the open question.

title: Should Rom 2:5 join the 'day of judgment' row?
now: Rom 2:5 ('the day of wrath, when God's righteous judgment will be revealed') stands in 'Judgment and works, deeds' and in 'The LORD's justice and judgments' but not in 'The day of judgment, the hour of judgment...'.
after: Rom 2:5 also appears in the day-of-judgment row and stays in the other two.
why: Rom 2:5 puts a day and a judgment in one clause ('the day of wrath, when God's righteous judgment will be revealed'), and no reader argued against it.

title: Should 'a kingdom of priests' get its own row?
now: Exod 19:6 ('a kingdom of priests') stands in the row 'Israel's and Judah's own kingdom', and Rev 1:6 and 5:10 stand in 'Given, taken away, thrown out, restored', whose heading says 'a kingdom, priests'.
after: No change.
why: The two rows already quote 'a kingdom of priests' (Exod 19:6) and 'a kingdom, priests' (Rev 1:6), and the page has 27 rows against an aim of 15 to 25, so a three-verse row goes the wrong way.

title: Should Ps 45:6 leave the row on the LORD's kingdom?
now: Ps 45:6 ('Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom') stands in both 'One king's kingdom, realm or sovereignty' and 'The LORD's kingdom, and the LORD over every kingdom', and each note says readers part on whom the psalm is spoken to.
after: No change.
why: Heb 1:8 quotes the verse 'about the Son', and a New Testament writer's use of an Old Testament verse is a reading, so keeping Ps 45:6 in both rows with the note takes no side where removing it would settle the matter.

title: Should the LORD's kingdom row name the verb 'reigns'?
now: The page holds only the noun 'kingdom'; the Hebrew verb 'reigns' (Ps 93:1, 97:1, 99:1) is left out on purpose, and the note under 'The LORD's kingdom, and the LORD over every kingdom' does not say so.
after: A sentence goes into that note: the Hebrew verb for 'reigns' ('The LORD reigns', Ps 93:1; 97:1; 99:1) is a different word from the nouns on this page, is not on it, and stands on the page 'The LORD reigns'.
why: Ps 93:1 ('The LORD reigns!') is the verb a reader of the Hebrew Scriptures looks for first, and a sentence that names it as a different word equates nothing and takes no side.

title: Should the Son row say Heb 1:8 quotes Ps 45:6?
now: The row 'Of the Son, of Christ' lists Heb 1:8 ('But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever...”'), and its note does not say that this is a quotation of Ps 45:6 or that Ps 45:6 stands in two other rows.
after: A sentence goes into the note under that row: Heb 1:8 reads 'But about the Son He says' and quotes Ps 45:6, which is also in the rows on one king's kingdom and the LORD's kingdom; readers part on whom the psalm is spoken to, and the page does not choose.
why: Heb 1:8 itself says 'But about the Son He says', so the note states only what the verse says and where the quoted verse is also placed.

title: Should the two rows on the LORD as light be joined?
now: Under 'What the text says of light', the row 'The LORD is my light, God is light, the LORD will be your everlasting light, the Light of Israel' (6 verses: Ps 27:1, Mic 7:8, Isa 60:19, 60:20, 1 John 1:5, Isa 10:17) and the row 'Light about God: “in Your light we see light”, “wraps Himself in light”, “the light of Your face”, “Father of the heavenly lights”' (9 verses: Ps 4:6, 36:9, 43:3, 44:3, 89:15, 90:8, 104:2, Hab 3:4, Jas 1:17) are two rows.
after: They become one row of 15 verses headed with the verses' own words, 'The LORD is my light'; 'God is light'; 'in Your light we see light'; 'He wraps Himself in light'; 'the light of Your face', with both notes kept and a sentence that the page does not say whether 'light' names what God is or what He has or gives; the page goes from 25 rows to 24, and 'Father of the heavenly lights' leaves the heading (Jas 1:17 is dealt with separately).
why: Ps 27:1 ('The LORD is my light') and 1 John 1:5 ('God is light') sit beside Ps 36:9 ('in Your light we see light') and Ps 104:2 ('He wraps Himself in light'), and the text draws no line between being and having light, so two rows lay out a position on it.

title: Should Isa 10:16 be shown beside Isa 10:17?
now: Isa 10:17 ('the Light of Israel will become a fire, and its Holy One a flame') is in the row 'The LORD is my light, God is light...', and the note under the row only says that the 'Light of Israel' becomes a fire; Isa 10:16, which names 'the Lord GOD of Hosts', is not shown.
after: Isa 10:16 is listed beside Isa 10:17 in the row, and the note says that 10:16 names 'the Lord GOD of Hosts' and 10:17 goes straight on with 'the Light of Israel' and 'its Holy One', so the pair is read together; the note no longer says the verse names no one.
why: Isa 10:16 reads 'the Lord GOD of Hosts will send' and 10:17 goes straight on with 'the Light of Israel' and, in the Hebrew, 'his Holy One', so under the new rule the verse beside it names him.

title: Where should Jas 1:17, 'Father of the lights', stand?
now: Jas 1:17 stands in the row 'Light about God', whose heading quotes 'Father of the heavenly lights'; the Greek is πατρὸς τῶν φώτων, 'Father of lights', with no word for 'heavenly', and the verse is not in the 'Sun, moon and stars' row.
after: Jas 1:17 is not put in the sun, moon and stars row. A sentence goes into the note of the God-light row (or of the joined row, if the two are merged): the Greek says 'the Father of the lights' and 'heavenly' is the Berean's word; readers take 'the lights' as the lights God set in the sky (Gen 1:14, where the Hebrew word is a different one) or as light itself, and the page does not choose. The missing 'heavenly' is recorded as a translation finding.
why: The Berean's 'heavenly' has no Greek word behind it, so listing the verse under the sky lights would rest on the translation's addition and decide the point.

title: Does John 12:35 need a note saying it names Jesus?
now: John 12:35 and 12:36 stand in the row 'Jesus: “I am the light of the world”, “the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ”', and the note under the row does not say why 12:35-36 are there.
after: No change.
why: John 12:35 itself reads 'Then Jesus told them', so the verse names Jesus and needs no note pointing to 12:36.

title: Should Ps 72:14 leave one of its two blood rows?
now: Ps 72:14 ('He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their blood is precious in his sight') stands in two rows: the one headed 'Blood avenged and required...' and the one headed 'Redeemed, purchased, released...'. The note under each row says what the blood is in that place.
after: No change.
why: The verse has the Hebrew word for 'redeem' (the root of the avenger's word) and 'their blood is precious in his sight', so it fits both rows, and 'He' is the king of the psalm (Ps 72:1), so the new pronoun rule does not move it.

title: Should the 'His blood' verses move into the row about Christ's blood?
now: The row headed 'The blood of Christ, of Jesus, of the Son, of the Lamb' shows only verses that name him (Heb 9:14, 1 John 1:7, 1 Pet 1:19, Rev 7:14 and others). A separate row headed ''His blood', 'His own blood', 'Your blood': the verse names no one' shows Rom 3:25, 5:9, Eph 1:7, Col 1:20, Heb 9:12, Acts 20:28 and Rev 5:9, and its note says the passage around them names Christ.
after: Rom 3:25, Rom 5:9, Eph 1:7, Heb 9:12 and Rev 5:9 move into the Christ row, each shown together with the verse beside it that answers the pronoun (Rom 3:24-25, 5:8-9, Eph 1:6-7, Heb 9:11-12, Rev 5:8-9), and that row's note says each verse names him or the verse beside it does. The 'His blood' row keeps only Col 1:20 and Acts 20:28, with its label and note reworded to say that the verse beside Col 1:20 does not name him and that Acts 20:28 names God and is read two ways; both verses still stand in their other rows too.
why: Rom 3:24 says 'Christ Jesus' just before 3:25 'God presented Him ... in His blood', Rom 5:8 says 'Christ died for us' just before 5:9 'justified by His blood', Heb 9:11 says 'Christ came as high priest' just before 9:12 'His own blood', and Rev 5:8 says 'the Lamb' just before 5:9 'by Your blood', so each pronoun is answered right beside it, while Col 1:19 only says 'Him' again.

title: Should the Jesus-and-wisdom note point back to 1 Cor 1:19-31?
now: The note under the row headed 'Jesus and wisdom...' explains 1 Cor 1:24 and 1:30 but says nothing of the verses before them. The row on 'The wisdom of the wise, of the nations and of this age' already has a note pointing forward to this row.
after: The note under the Jesus row gets one more sentence: 1 Cor 1:19-31 runs from the row on the wisdom of the wise (1:19 quotes Isa 29:14, 1:20 asks where the wise are and says God has made foolish the wisdom of the world) to 1:24 and 1:30 here, and the page does not say how they relate. No verse moves.
why: 1 Cor 1:20 ('Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?') and 1:24 ('Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God') are one argument shown in two rows, and the pointer back makes no claim.

title: Should the Spirit-and-wisdom row be split by Old and New Testament?
now: One row headed 'The Spirit of God and wisdom...' shows nine verses: Exod 28:3, 31:3, 35:31, Deut 34:9 and Isa 11:2, then Acts 6:3, 6:10, Eph 1:17 and 1 Cor 12:8. The whole row links to the card on the Holy Spirit, and its note quotes each phrase as written ('the Spirit of God', 'a spirit of wisdom', 'the Spirit and wisdom') and says readers part on whether it names the Holy Spirit.
after: No change.
why: Whether 'a spirit of wisdom' (Deut 34:9, Eph 1:17) or 'the Spirit of God' (Exod 31:3) names the Holy Spirit is a reading, not a pronoun that a nearby verse answers, so the new rule does not apply and the note already says so.

title: Should the wrath note keep citing Rom 1:24, 26 and 28?
now: Under the first row, 'The anger of the LORD, the wrath of God', the note says readers part on whether God's wrath is his own response to evil or what sin brings with it, and puts '(Rom 1:24, 26, 28 say three times that God 'gave them over')' in brackets after the second reading. Those three verses stand in no row, because they have no word for wrath.
after: The three verses still get no row. The note is reworded so the citation belongs to neither reading: Rom 1:18 says the wrath of God 'is being revealed'; the verses after it say God 'gave them over' (1:24, 26) and 'gave them up' (1:28), the same Greek verb each time, with no word for wrath. The sentence that readers part on what the wrath is, and that the page takes no side, stays.
why: Rom 1:24 and 1:26 read 'God gave them over' and 1:28 reads 'He gave them up', with no word for wrath, so they cannot be shown in a wrath row, and the brackets lean toward the second reading.

title: Should the wrath hub drop a row to reach 25?
now: The wrath hub shows 26 rows (24 on the noun, 2 on the verb), one over the 15 to 25 aimed for. The rows that look alike are the two prayer rows and the three rows on human anger.
after: No change.
why: The two prayer rows ask opposite things ('O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger', Ps 6:1; 'Pour out Your wrath on the nations', Ps 79:6) and the human-anger rows differ by who speaks (Prov 15:1; Eph 4:26), so no two rows say one thing twice.

title: Should readings 1 and 2 on tongues swap places?
now: The card 'Speaking in tongues' shows first 'The gifts continue', then 'The sign gifts have ended', then 'The Spirit may give the gift today'. A hidden note says the order follows when each reading was first set out.
after: No change.
why: No verse says which reading came first (the readings turn on Acts 2:4 and 1 Cor 13:8), and either order would claim that one arrived before the other.

title: Should reading 1 name the multiracial start of Pentecostalism?
now: The summary of reading 1 describes Pentecostal and Charismatic practice (tongues in private prayer, in worship, and the teaching called initial evidence) and says nothing of where the movement began or who first practised it.
after: No change.
why: No verse backs a sentence about the movement's beginnings (the reading rests on Acts 2:39 and 19:6), and naming one church in one reading while the other readings name none would tilt the page.

title: Should reading 1 include 1 Cor 14:18, 'more than all of you'?
now: Reading 1 shows eight verses, four of them from chapter 14 (14:2, 14:4, 14:14 and 14:39). 1 Cor 14:18 is not shown.
after: No change.
why: Reading 1 already carries 14:39 ('do not forbid speaking in tongues') beside 14:4, so chapter 14 is not shown only from the regulating side, and a ninth verse would leave the three readings uneven.

title: Should reading 2 on tongues include Heb 2:4 and 2 Cor 12:12?
now: Reading 2 ('The sign gifts have ended') shows eight verses, among them two separate rows for 1 Cor 14:21 (the 'strange tongues' saying, with a note that Paul takes it from Isa 28:11-12) and 14:22 ('Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers').
after: Heb 2:4 is shown in reading 2, quoted 'and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.' with the note 'Read as signs that affirmed the message at its first preaching.' The separate row for 1 Cor 14:21 is removed and its Isaiah note moves under 1 Cor 14:22, so reading 2 stays at eight verses. 2 Cor 12:12 is not shown.
why: Heb 2:4 ('affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit') is the one verse that says the signs affirmed the first preaching, though it does not use the word tongues, while 2 Cor 12:12 ('The marks of a true apostle') names neither tongues nor the Spirit's gifts.

title: Should reading 2 swap Rom 11:6 for Gen 15:6?
now: Reading 2 ('By faith alone') shows eight verses, among them Rom 11:6 ('if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works'). Gen 15:6 is quoted only inside the notes on Rom 4:3 (reading 2) and James 2:23 (reading 1).
after: No change.
why: Rom 11:6 ('it is no longer by works') carries the reading's claim that works add nothing, and Gen 15:6 ('it was credited to him as righteousness') filed under one reading would be heard only through Paul.

title: Should a new term entry set out Abraham and Gen 15:6?
now: The card lists eight terms (sola fide, imputed righteousness, merit, synergy and others) and none on Abraham, so Gen 15:6 shows only inside the notes on Rom 4:3 and James 2:23.
after: A ninth term, 'Abraham and Genesis 15:6', is shown: Paul (Rom 4:3) and James (James 2:23) both quote Gen 15:6, 'Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness'; the readings differ on whether it shows righteousness credited for believing before any work or a faith that Abraham's later obedience completed (James 2:22). It quotes Gen 22:12 (the angel of the LORD, 22:11-12) and Gen 26:5 (the LORD to Isaac, 26:2-5) as speaking of Abraham's fear of God and obedience, and says the Hebrew of 15:6 has the active verb 'he reckoned it to him' without saying who reckoned. The sentence beginning 'Jewish readers take' is left out, and Rom 11:6 stays in reading 2.
why: Gen 15:6 ('it was credited to him as righteousness'), 22:12 ('you fear God') and 26:5 ('Abraham listened to My voice') say what the entry says, but no verse says how Jewish readers take them and no rabbi's seat has confirmed it.

title: Should Eph 1:11 be shown in reading 2 on God's choosing?
now: Reading 2 (God's choice resting on his own purpose) shows eight verses, among them Eph 1:5 ('He predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ') and Acts 13:48 ('all who were appointed for eternal life believed'). Eph 1:11 appears only in the note on the word 'predestined', and John 15:16 is not shown.
after: No change.
why: Eph 1:11 ('predestined according to the plan of Him who works out everything') repeats Eph 1:5, the Greek behind its 'chosen' means 'obtained an inheritance', and John 15:16 ('You did not choose Me, but I chose you') is said to the disciples about being sent to bear fruit.

title: Should Rom 11:32 and Rom 11:5 be shown in readings 1 and 3?
now: Reading 1 shows eight verses (1 Tim 2:4, 2 Pet 3:9, John 3:16 and others) and reading 3 shows eight, among them Rom 9:6 and Rom 11:28. Neither shows Rom 11:32 or Rom 11:5.
after: No change.
why: Rom 11:32 ('God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone') in one reading alone would read as the hope-for-all verse, and Rom 11:5 ('a remnant chosen by grace') would need a verse taken out of an even eight, with 11:28 already carrying Israel's standing.

title: Should reading 1 on hell name Augsburg Confession Article 17?
now: Reading 1 ('Punishment without end') says Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican, Wesleyan, Baptist, Pentecostal and Anabaptist teaching each state the reading in their own way. No confession is named.
after: No change.
why: The proposed wording was not checked against the Augsburg text, and naming one confession for one tradition and none for the other eight would tip the page.

title: Should 2 Pet 3:9 leave the agreed block on hell?
now: The agreed block at the top says every reading takes the text to say 'that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked and wants everyone to come to repentance', and shows five verses: Gen 18:25, Heb 9:27, Ezek 33:11, 2 Pet 3:9 and Rev 20:12.
after: The summary reads only 'that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked', and 2 Pet 3:9 is no longer shown in the agreed block, which keeps Ezek 33:11 and shows four verses. 2 Pet 3:9 is not moved into any reading; 1 Tim 2:4 already stands in reading 2.
why: 2 Pet 3:9 reads 'not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance', and the election card records holders who read 'everyone' as every kind of person, so it is not common ground for every reading here.

title: Should Matt 5:18 be shown with Matt 5:17 in the Sabbath readings?
now: Reading 1 and reading 3 each show Matt 5:17 as 'Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets.' and stop there, so 'but to fulfill them' and Matt 5:18 are not shown. The paragraph where reading 2 answers the others says Jesus fulfils the Law.
after: Reading 1 and reading 3 each show Matt 5:17-18 whole: 'Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them. For I tell you truly, until heaven and earth pass away, not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen, will disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished.' Each keeps its own note, and reading 2's answering paragraph also quotes 'until everything is accomplished' beside 'fulfill'. Each reading stays at eight verses; the quote check must be run to confirm a verse range is accepted.
why: Matt 5:17 as now quoted stops before 'but to fulfill them', and 5:18 ('until everything is accomplished') is the half all three readings argue over, so showing the saying whole in both readings that carry it tilts nothing.

title: Should the stated basis for the order of the Sabbath readings change?
now: The readings run: the seventh day kept, fulfilled in Christ, the Lord's Day. A hidden note explains the order as the practice of the first believers for the first reading and the dates each reading was set out for the others; the basis shows nowhere on the page itself.
after: The three readings stay in the same order and nothing a reader sees changes. The hidden note stops calling the seventh-day reading the practice of the first believers and says instead that the readings follow the question's own steps (the command stands as given; it is fulfilled in Christ; it stands, moved to the first day), that no dating is claimed, and that the order is not a ranking. The proposed basis, 'when each reading is first set down in writing', is not used.
why: Col 2:16-17 and Heb 4:9 do not say which reading came first, so the page should not claim a date basis, and the proposed replacement would put the fulfilment reading before the seventh-day reading.

title: Should reading 1 on tithing cite Westminster Confession 19.4?
now: Reading 1 ('Giving freely') says some Reformed teachers take the tithe to belong to the law's ceremonial and civil order, resting on Heb 7:5 and 7:12. No confession is cited.
after: No change.
why: The chapter could not be checked here, and as recalled it speaks of Israel's civil laws expiring without naming the tithe, so the card would credit the confession with a view it does not state.

title: Should the Mal 3:10 note show the blessing words?
now: Reading 2 ('The tenth still stands') quotes Mal 3:10 as 'Bring the full tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in My house.' Its note says the verse 'goes on to words of blessing, which the readings take differently for Israel and for readers now'.
after: The quote stays as it is. The note instead shows the words: 'The command to bring the whole tithe. The verse goes on: “Test Me in this,” says the LORD of Hosts. “See if I will not open the windows of heaven and pour out for you blessing without measure.” It is spoken to Israel, and the readings take it differently for Israel and for readers now.'
why: Mal 3:10 does go on 'Test Me in this ... pour out for you blessing without measure', so a note saying only 'words of blessing' hides what the verse says, but putting those words in the quoted passage itself would imply a return on giving.

title: Should Acts 16:34 be shown in reading 3 on baptism?
now: Reading 3 ('Baptism of those who believe') shows eight verses and Acts 16:34 is not one of them, though the paragraph where reading 3 answers the others cites it for the household rejoicing in believing. Reading 1 shows Acts 16:33 ('he and all his household were baptized').
after: No change.
why: The Berean has 'he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God', but the Greek word for believing (pepisteukos) is singular, so the plural rests on the Berean alone and the answering paragraph's use of the verse should be checked against the Greek separately.

title: Should reading 2 swap John 6:39 for Phil 2:13?
now: Reading 2 ('The perseverance of the saints') shows eight verses, among them John 10:28, John 6:39 ('that I shall lose none of those He has given Me'), Rom 8:39, Phil 1:6 and 1 Pet 1:5. Its summary says the warnings are the means God uses to keep his people, and no shown verse says so; Heb 6:9 is not shown.
after: John 6:39 is no longer shown in reading 2 and Phil 2:13 takes its place, quoted 'For it is God who works in you to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose.' with the note 'Read with 2:12 as working out salvation while God works in the believer.' Rom 8:39 stays, John 6:39 is still cited by number in reading 1's answering paragraph, and reading 2 stays at eight verses.
why: Phil 2:12-13 ('work out your salvation ... for it is God who works in you') is the one pair that shows the warning and God's keeping together, and John 10:28 ('they will never perish') already says what John 6:39 says.

title: Should a 'chiliasm' term place Anabaptist churches in no reading?
now: The end-times card shows four readings (premillennial, amillennial, preterist, postmillennial) and none lists an Anabaptist church. Its terms include none on the older word chiliasm.
after: No change.
why: Rev 20:4-5 ('they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years') names no church, so what Anabaptist writers teach about it cannot be checked from the verses, and the page says of no other tradition that it sits in no reading.

title: Should Oriental Orthodox be named in reading 1 on human nature?
now: Reading 1 ('Wounded and healed') is held by Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches, with a sentence on Eastern Orthodox teaching about ancestral sin. Oriental Orthodox churches are named nowhere, as on every other card.
after: No change.
why: Rom 5:12 ('death was passed on to all men, because all sinned') and 1 Cor 15:22 do not say which church holds the reading, and naming them on this one card would make it differ from every other card, so the right route is one change to the shared list of traditions, queued as a plan proposal.
